title: What You Trace is What You Get: Dynamic Stack-Layout Recovery for Binary Recompilation
problem: Binary recompilers cannot recover local variables with sufficient precision in lifted programs using heuristic-based or conservative over-approximation approaches, which prevents application of compiler optimizations to legacy binaries without source code.
motivation: Users of proprietary and legacy programs need access to modern compiler technologies for optimization and analysis without vendor support or source code availability.
method: The approach uses dynamic tracing of binary execution to recover precise stack layouts and local variable locations. Runtime profiling information is collected during program execution to determine how the stack is organized, enabling accurate local variable identification in the lifted intermediate representation without relying on unreliable static heuristics.
key_novelty: Replacing static heuristics with dynamic runtime tracing to precisely recover stack layouts for local variable recovery in binary recompilation.
contributions: Dynamic stack-layout recovery technique using execution traces
Precise local variable identification in lifted binaries
Enabling compiler optimizations on binaries without source code
Elimination of imprecision from static heuristic and conservative approximation approaches
primary_theme: Dynamic stack-layout recovery for binary recompilation
